newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon MP wants Hariri, officials prosecuted.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon MP wants Hariri, officials prosecuted.

text.p: An opposition member of parliament accused Lebanon's billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and other officials on Tuesday of profiteering from a new media law and asked judicial authorities to prosecute them.
Leftist MP Najah Wakim said Hariri and the others had made "tens of millions of dollars in profits" by licensing their own television and radio stations last year while banning others.

"Parliament Speaker (Nabih) Berri, Prime Minister Hariri, his deputy (Michel al-) Murr and other ministers made big personal gains...through state funds they were entrusted to manage. They took advantage of their positions and hurt the public interest," he said in a document sent to Prosecutor-General Adnan Addoum. He sent a copy to Reuters.
The officials' actions infringed a law banning the illegal accumulation of wealth by holders of public office, he said.
Wakim, a Beirut deputy, asked the prosecutor to bring charges against the officials and revoke licences of radio and television stations they own directly or through associates.
Government officials were not immediately available to comment, but the government has said the licences were awarded in line with criteria set by a government-appointed committee.
Judicial sources said the prosecutor-general would review the accusations and decide whether to file charges or order investigations against the officials.

The government last year ordered the closure of scores of privately owned radio and television stations and granted licences to only four private television and 11 radio stations under a law regulating broadcast media.

Three of the four television stations granted licences are owned by Hariri, Berri and Murr or their associates. Of the three radio stations allowed to broadcast news two are owned by Hariri and Berri.

"They (Hariri, Berri, Murr) made big profits through licenses worth tens of millions of dollars while depriving others of similar benefits, and they monopolised the domestic advertising market and the satellite broadcasting market estimated to be worth an annual $400 million according to experts," Wakim's document said.
